text: That $100 ticket becomes $130 at checkout, that's no accident, it's called drip pricing.
The fees drip in at the very end.
In a StubHub experiment with millions of users, hiding fees until checkout made people spend
about 21% more, and they were about 14% more likely to buy at all.
By checkout, you've picked your seats, they already feel like yours.
So in May 2025, a U.S. rule made ticket sellers and hotels show the full price up front.
Taxes can still come later, but mandatory fees? No more surprises.
That's the mirage. The price you see first isn't the price. It's the bait.
So judge every deal by the total at checkout, not the number that hooked you.
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
